quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You have a green light. There are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross first.
You have the right to go before pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must let pedestrians cross. When turning on a green light, drivers must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: Bad weather or darkness requires you to turn on your lights. Which lights should you use?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
Do not turn left.
Do not make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn left.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and against the law to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Stop and let them cross.
Drive around them to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until they finish crossing before you drive.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only after a crash.
After a crash or when stopped for a traffic ticket.
Only when stopped for a traffic ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a crash or when stopped for a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when driving. Show it to an officer after a crash or when pulled over for a ticket.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, you should drive at:

options.text: The same speed as the other traffic on the freeway.
The posted speed limit.
A slower speed than the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as the other traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Enter a freeway at the same speed as traffic, unless traffic is speeding above the legal limit.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is correct?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speeds require more distance between you and the car ahead.
Both statements are correct.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both statements are correct.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. They also increase your stopping distance, so you need more space behind the car ahead of you.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions and no one can pass.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Mirrors on both sides eliminate blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Trucks have large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

questions.question: Drowsiness affects driving the same way alcohol does. It can:

options.text: Make you a better driver.
Make you feel better.
Affect your ability to think clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Affect your ability to think clearly.
questions.explanation: Sleep deprivation is dangerous. Like drugs and alcohol, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and affects your judgment.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: You can pass from both directions.
You can pass only from your direction.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow centerline means no one can cross it to pass, no matter which direction they are going.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass if you are next to the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass if you are next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if you are next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: The broken yellow line means you can pass. The solid yellow line means you cannot pass. So you can only pass from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They get shorter and less severe as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They get longer and more severe as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get longer and more severe as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more serious crashes.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
The driver who arrived first.
The driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go through in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Look in the inside rearview mirror.
Look in the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must turn and look over your shoulder to check them.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes are going the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates traffic going in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line on a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic is moving in opposite directions, and you cannot pass.
Traffic is moving in opposite directions, and you can pass.
Traffic is moving the same direction, and you cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in opposite directions, and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Solid lines mean no passing is allowed.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through intersections at this speed.
The maximum safe speed is 55 mph under normal conditions.
You must drive at least this fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed is 55 mph under normal conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You can drive slower when needed, but never faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to watch traffic behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to watch traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you know where nearby vehicles are at all times.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for someone or a vehicle to move into your lane suddenly.
Expect other drivers and pedestrians to stay out of your way.
Drive close to the parked cars to give moving traffic more room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for someone or a vehicle to move into your lane suddenly.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your car and parked vehicles. A person may step out without looking, or a parked car may start moving without warning.

questions.question: You can cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and theirs.
questions.explanation: Stay at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you risk hitting the rider if they fall. This is especially dangerous on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: If you must park your vehicle in an unusual spot:

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for keeping your parked vehicle safe. Make sure your car is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.

questions.question: This sign tells a driver that:

options.text: A construction worker with a flag is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A construction worker with a flag is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flag person is ahead. Always follow their directions. Flaggers wear bright orange, yellow, or yellow-green clothing. They use paddles and red flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the posted speed when the light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, proceed through the intersection with caution.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep the posted speed to make it through.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, wet leaves, ice, and oil. A dry, solid surface is safest for driving.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign is a traffic law sign. It tells drivers that making a U-turn is not permitted.

questions.question: If you parallel park facing downhill:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or edge of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb or edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road. When parking uphill without a curb, turn wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: Truck blind spots are:

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left of the cab.
On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Truck blind spots are much larger than car blind spots. The truck driver cannot see your vehicle if you are directly behind or to the left of the truck. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake suddenly to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops gradually and smoothly.
